entries.title: Psalms 137:1
segments:
PSALM CXXXVII. 
 
  Probably this psalm was wrote toward the end of the Babylonish   captivity.  Herein the captives complain of the scoffs of their   enemies, yet remember Jerusalem, and foresee the downfall of   Babylon, ver. 1-9. 
 
  V. 1. Sat-The usual posture of mourners.

entries.title: Psalms 137:2
segments: V. 2. Harps-Harps are here put for all instruments of musick.

entries.title: Psalms 137:3
segments: V. 3. A song-Such songs as you used to sing in the temple of Zion.

entries.title: Psalms 137:4
segments: V. 4. The Lord's-Those songs which were appointed by God to be sung only in his service.

entries.title: Psalms 137:6
segments: V. 6. If-If I do not value Jerusalem's prosperity more than all other delights.

entries.title: Psalms 137:7
segments: V. 7. The day-In the time of its destruction.

entries.title: Psalms 137:8
segments: V. 8. Happy-As being God's instrument to vindicate his honour, and execute his just judgments.
